item.title: Hiroshima Sake Festival: Saijo's Great October Tasting — Guide
item.description: The Sake Festival, held in Saijo over a weekend each October, is one of the largest sake events in Japan and turns the whole brewery town into a celebration. Its centrepiece is a huge tasting hall where, for a single ticket, visitors can sample from hundreds of labels gathered from breweries the length of the country — an extraordinary opportunity to compare regional styles side by side. Outside, Saijo’s own historic breweries open their courtyards, food stalls fill the streets between the red-brick chimneys, and stages host music.

item.title: Osaka Sake & Izakaya Tasting: A Night of Drinking Osaka — Guide
item.description: Osaka takes drinking as seriously as eating, and a night in its izakaya and sake bars is one of the warmest experiences the city offers. The options run from tachinomi standing bars crammed under railway arches around Umeda and Namba, where a few hundred yen buys a glass and a skewer, to specialist sake bars pouring flights from breweries across the Kansai region and English-friendly guided tastings that walk you through junmai, ginjo and the differences between them.

item.title: Chichibu Whisky & Craft Sake: A World-Renowned Distilling Region — Guide
item.description: The Chichibu Distillery, founded in 2008, has rapidly become one of the most acclaimed craft whisky producers in the world, its single malt expressions winning international awards and commanding premium prices among collectors. The distillery uses locally grown barley and traditional techniques, including its own cooperage for barrel-making, a rarity even in Scotland. Chichibu’s mountain water and cool climate have also long supported local sake breweries and craft beer producers, making the area a broader destination for spirits and brewing enthusiasts.

item.title: Orion Beer Guide: Brewery Tour, Tasting & Access (Nago)
item.description: Orion Beer is Okinawa’s hometown brew — a crisp, easy-drinking lager designed for the island’s heat and humidity, and a fixture of every izakaya table and beach barbecue. Founded in Nago in 1957, Orion is a beloved symbol of Okinawan identity. At the Nago brewery (Orion Happy Park) you can tour the production line and reward yourself with a glass of ultra-fresh draft straight from the source — a fun, family-friendly stop in northern Okinawa, often combined with the aquarium.

item.title: Yoichi Nikka Whisky Distillery Guide: Tour, Tasting & Access
item.description: The Yoichi Nikka Whisky Distillery, on the coast just beyond Otaru, is the birthplace of one of Japan’s most storied whiskies — and a pilgrimage for whisky lovers. Founded in 1934 by Masataka Taketsuru, “the father of Japanese whisky,” who chose Yoichi for its Scotland-like climate, the distillery still uses traditional coal-fired pot stills. The handsome stone-and-ivy grounds (the setting of a famous NHK drama) house the working distillery, a whisky museum and a tasting bar.
